s: a tiny piazza kiosk punching above its size with natural wine and serious coffee
w: A humble kiosk in the middle of Piazzale degli Eroi that's built a following well beyond its footprint -- specialty coffee from strong Roman roasters, a genuine natural wine list, aperitivo and canned cocktails, all taken standing in the piazza with neighbours. Coffee here feels considered rather than incidental, in a kiosk format that could easily have settled for less.
_facts: Located at Piazzale degli Eroi, 00136 Roma, in the Prati neighbourhood near the Vatican
Started as a small kiosk bar in the piazza, now known for its natural wine list alongside specialty coffee
Serves aperitivo and canned cocktails as well as coffee
Functions as a standing, piazza-based social spot rather than a seated café

s: a three-floor bookshop-café under a frescoed 17th-century ceiling
w: A bookshop spread across three floors of the 1676 Palazzo Cavallerini Lazzaroni, connected by an exposed metal-railed staircase, with a small café on the second floor sitting under an elaborately frescoed ceiling. The building previously housed a well-known design and furniture showroom before its current life as a literary, art-adjacent hideaway a few steps from Piazza Argentina.
_facts: Located at Via dei Barbieri 7, 00186 Roma, near Piazza Argentina
Housed in the Palazzo Cavallerini Lazzaroni, built 1676 by architect Giovanni Antonio De Rossi
Three-floor independent bookshop with a small second-floor café under a frescoed ceiling
The building previously housed a design and furniture showroom

s: a working-class market rebuilt over first-century Roman warehouses
w: A clean, well-organised covered market sitting atop the remains of 1st-century Roman warehouses, where locals shop for produce and grab ready-to-eat food from stalls known city-wide -- panini and supplì, creative pizza al taglio, and other no-nonsense bites. A genuine neighbourhood institution, rebuilt on its current site in 2012, that feels nothing like a tourist food court.
_facts: Located at Via Aldo Manuzio, 00153 Roma, Testaccio
Current market building opened in 2012, replacing the older market on nearby Piazza Testaccio
Built over and incorporating remains of 1st-century Roman warehouse structures
Known for standout street-food stalls (panini, supplì, pizza al taglio) alongside grocery vendors

s: the no-frills Trastevere bar that's been the neighbourhood's heartbeat for decades
w: A plain, unpretentious bar on Piazza di San Calisto that has anchored bohemian Trastevere for generations -- artists, writers, students and old-timers all take their espresso, cappuccino or afternoon glass of wine at the same handful of outdoor tables. No design, no concept, just the kind of everyday institution that outlasts every trend around it.
_facts: Located at Piazza di San Calisto 3, 00153 Roma, Trastevere
Long-running, old-school neighbourhood bar with a mixed local/bohemian following
Known for cheap, no-frills coffee and drinks rather than any design concept
